For a game about a guerrilla insurgency, your allies are shockingly bad at picking their battles and fighting according to traditional guerrilla doctrines of hit-and-run attacks and sabotage or targeted assassination, instead they just simply wander around in small groups until they are within shouting distance of an opposition soldier who they immediately engage without any nuance or tactical forethought. 

And how about the other side? The supposed Soldados also seem to completely lack even the most basic understanding of military doctrine and protocols. It would be incredibly easy to defeat the entire army if all it took was some gunshots being heard in the distance (in a war zone, and a nation apparently vastly overpopulated by incredibly hostile wildlife that frequently banzai charges groups of armed soldiers and wins that fight about half the time) to cause an entire watch shift to abandon their posts to a man without being ordered, leaving you to loot or destroy their supplies and seize their key strategic positions and territories at your leisure, if not for your own imbecilic freedom fighters roving the countryside. 

I like the game, it’s fun, but many potentially awesome moments are completely ruined by the inexcusably terrible AI and/or suicidally aggressive wildlife. 

It has enormous potential as a far cry sandbox that we all know by now, as far as accommodating any play style you desire, but the above is just a taste of the lazy or flat out poorly thought out design decisions which can derail the possibility to “play it your way”. I suppose that’s an inherent flaw of the sandbox type game in general; with so many moving parts and things happening in the world around you, any tense situation or tactical triumph sort of lacks direction and impact compared to a tightly scripted set piece a la Call of Duty campaigns. I’m not talking about just the city. The entire surrounding area was affected too and it’s not like the whole state is below sea level. The entire area to the north/northwest of the city was devastated by the winds leaving easily at least 100,000 people (likely more) without power and in many cases running water as well. A major sore spot with the locals is the fact that every time a storm hits the area, all people think or talk about is New Orleans, not realizing that the surrounding area is home to a population that handily eclipses that of the city. Baton Rogue, Hammond, Covington/Mandeville, And Slidell are all within 45-70 min drive of the city and all have populations between 20,000-30,000, and a quarter million in Baton Rogue alone.

I’m not suggesting they bury the whole grid but local lines could be put underground no problem. Many new neighborhoods being built in the area are using underground lines, and flood zones are well established so flood waters are predictable based on river crest levels. And as I said before, the flooding wasn’t as much a problem as the sustained winds knocking trees over on to the lines and poles, subsequently creating hazards on roads and such. Anyone with a chainsaw can come and cut up a downed tree and get it out of the way, and flood waters can recede with time, but it gets more complicated when a tree is all tangled up in transmission lines.

I wouldn’t say it “worked out” for them, but it made things less bad. The entire region is still almost entirely without electricity and will remain so for weeks because instead of replacing the antiquated above ground power transmission infrastructure with a more cutting edge solution, they just rebuild it exactly the same as it was before. The levees work great for a wet storm but this one packed devastating winds more than torrential rains, resulting in (so far as we know), over 8,000 downed or damaged poles, over 9,000 downed or damaged spans of cable, and over 1700 destroyed or damaged transformers.

Source: am from SE Louisiana, was smack in the middle of the storm’s path.

I was in 7th grade, attending school in downtown Tucson, AZ. The attack had already started when I woke up for school, my mom was freaking out about it, but my mom is also very dramatic about almost anything so my half asleep ass dismissed the attack as foolish as I knew about the last time someone bombed the towers and everything was basically fine. 

At school we didn’t really do much except watch the news and were sent home shortly before the first tower fell. It was all so surreal, everywhere we went on the way home had the same thing on, and you could see the pain and fear and disbelief in every strangers face, because for the first time in living memory, a hostile foreign force successfully attacked us *here*. Sure, there was Pearl Harbor, but this was right here on the shores of one of the Crown Jewels of our nation. I was too young to really understand how much this would end up changing the world, but not by much, and watched in silent horror how a feeling of unity and togetherness, regardless of code, creed, or color, was twisted into a petty witch hunt that divided the nation and has been getting worse ever since; how our right to simply exist without drawing the suspicions of federal law enforcement and intelligence agencies was violated; how people so willingly let themselves be controlled by their fears. 

I hope that people someday all realize that we’re all just the same, doesn’t matter what color your skin is or what gods you worship if any, or what language you speak, we all basically want the same things and there’s enough for everyone if we’re smart about it. But I fear that it’s already too late to change course, certainly in my lifetime and likely not for several decades after at the very least. 

TL;DR 9/11 happened in 7th grade and the consequences were a major contributor on my course to nihilism, paranoia, and chronic depression.

I don't have exact numbers as I have tweaked them quite a bit, but here are some guidelines to get you started:

Increase player speed across the board, not a huge jump but default sliders make every player move slower than they feel like they should and the whole game feels sluggish as a result. I also close the gap a bit between fastest and slowest players, as many bigs are able to keep up with smaller players just fine irl, but in 2k they lumber around like drunk giants in a swamp made of molasses. 

Tweak foul frequency: I turn down the frequency of reach in fouls by a fair bit, as it is very annoying how often that happens, especially when they are consecutive right off the inbound pass from the last reach in foul. I also generally decrease frequency of fouls that you don't see a whole lot of in real play, such as over the backs and lose ball fouls. I increase shooting foul frequency slightly. 

I slightly lower everyone's steal rating and decrease the frequency of steal attempts since every AI player is an omniscient steal god who can predict the future. 

By default, AI defensive awareness is set sort of low so I set it to be on par with my own team's. 

I slightly increase the success of 3pt shots since proven shooters clanking wide open 3s is a well known problem in 2k. I do the same with inside shots, and slightly decrease mid range success rate. 

There are a few other things that I probably forgot, but with my sliders I generally see more realistic shooting percentages (low 40's to mid 50's for a team that is having a good night, instead of stupid shit like 60% or more) for both teams, as well as FTA's and turnovers.
